newsitem.title: GERMANY: Turkish father detained in German arson case.
newsitem.headline: Turkish father detained in German arson case.

text.p: German police have detained the father of a Turkish family father on suspicion of starting a fire in which his wife and two children died and which has strained relations with Turkey, a spokesman said on Friday.

State prosecutors in the town of Krefeld said the 42-year-old was strongly suspected of starting the fire, which took place on Sunday night, and that more details would be given at a news conference later in the day.

Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan has angered Germany by blaming the attack, together with a suspected racist firebombing in the Netherlands in which six Turks died, on rising anti-Moslem sentiment in the West.
Police in Krefeld have suspected arson from the outset but said there was no evidence to suggest a racially motivated attack.

The man's 41-year-old wife was fatally injured when she jumped from their third-floor flat in a high-rise block in the town centre. A 16-year-old daughter died in hospital from her injuries and a 17-year-old son was found dead in the building.
Two female members of the family, aged 19 and 16, also jumped out of the flat and were severely injured.
On Thursday the German government summoned Turkey's ambassador to protest at criticism from Ankara suggesting that Germany was not doing enough to protect its immigrant population.

Turkey's Interior Minister Meral Aksener was quoted by the semi-official Anatolian news agency as saying in Turkey on Thursday that "they (Germans) couldn't throw us out, now they are trying to burn us out".
German Interior Minister Manfred Kanther said he was "extremely astonished" at the reported remarks and urged Turkey to reject them "immediately and unequivocally".
